items.t: Introduced a bill in the Vermont legislature that would ban cellphone use by people under the age of 21.
items.q: A Vermont state senator looking to make a point about cellphone use is calling for people under the age of 21 to face $1,000 fines and jail time if they are caught using the devices. Sen. John Rodgers, a Democrat, has introduced a bill to the state legislature that would ban cellphones for anybody under the legal drinking age.

record.t: Lost the November 3, 2026 general election for Lieutenant Governor of Vermont to Molly Gray.
record.q: Molly Gray (D) defeated incumbent John Rodgers (R) in the general election for Lieutenant Governor of Vermont on November 3, 2026.

record.t: Assumed office as Lieutenant Governor of Vermont on January 9, 2025, with a current term ending January 7, 2027.
record.q: John Rodgers (Republican Party) is the Lieutenant Governor of Vermont. He assumed office on January 9, 2025. His current term ends on January 7, 2027.

record.t: Was elected Lieutenant Governor of Vermont in the November 5, 2024 general election, defeating incumbent David Zuckerman and Ian Diamondstone.
record.q: John Rodgers (R) defeated incumbent David Zuckerman (Vermont Progressive Party / D) and Ian Diamondstone (Green Mountain Peace and Justice Party of Vermont) in the general election for Lieutenant Governor of Vermont on November 5, 2024.

record.t: Proposed a bill that would ban the use and possession of cellphones for anyone under 21.
record.q: A proposed bill, introduced by Vermont state Sen. John Rodgers, a Democrat, seeks to ban the use and possession of cellphones for anyone under 21.
